P.expected_type: ∀ {V : Type} [instVAdd : AddCommGroup V] [instVMod : Module ℂ V] (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (K : Type) [instK : Field K] (x : Module.End ℂ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (h_H001 : Nat.Prime p ∧ CharP K p) (h_H002 : 0 ≤ lam ∧ lam < (p : ℤ)) (h_H003 : Module.Finite ℂ V ∧ Module.finrank ℂ V = (lam + 1).toNat ∧ h * x - x * h = (2 : ℂ) • x ∧ h * y - y * h = (-2 : ℂ) • y ∧ x * y - y * x = h ∧ Highest lam x h ∧ Simple x y h) (h_H004 : v ≠ 0 ∧ x v = 0 ∧ h v = (lam : ℂ) • v) (h_H005 : Admissible M x y), Target K M x y h

correspondence.explanation: For arbitrary prime p, arbitrary field K with CharP K p, integer 0≤λ<p, the given finite-dimensional complex irreducible highest-weight module and vector, and any admissible lattice M, H001–H005 encode the original hypotheses. The three endomorphisms give the Chevalley action through the relations [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=−2y, [x,y]=h; their invariant complex subspaces are exactly the sl₂-submodules, so Highest plus Simple describes the stated irreducible highest-weight module. H005 asserts the original integer/complex basis condition and all divided-power stability, equivalently U_Z-stability. There is no minimal-lattice assumption. Tensor commutation m⊗c↦c⊗m identifies source M⊗ℤK with VK; its inverse swaps factors and it intertwines all extended lattice operators. Target existentially constructs their restrictions a, requiring Agrees on every m∈M, so each restriction is unique and is the original lattice action. Conversely the original induced action supplies such a. Simple explicitly says Nontrivial VK and universally quantifies every K-submodule W with the three invariance hypotheses and conclusion W=⊥ or W=⊤. This is equivalent to the whole stated target because the three abstract Chevalley generators span L(K), including at p=2. No distinct reduced weights, algebraic closure, or positive λ is assumed; λ=0 remains allowed. Restriction existence is already a derived N002 obligation, not a new premise.
